newsitem.title: USA: MAF says Q1 EPS could beat analysts' view.
newsitem.headline: MAF says Q1 EPS could beat analysts' view.

text.p: MAF Bancorp Inc said Tuesday its first quarter earnings could be somewhat better than analysts' estimates of $0.78 a share.

"I don't think we'll have any problem with $0.78. We could do somewhat better than that," chief executive officer Allen Koranda said following a presentation at a Howe Barnes Investments Inc conference here.
He also called analysts' estimates of $3.30-$3.40 a share for the year "numbers that we're comfortable with."
Comparable figures for 1996 are not applicable, because the company acquired NS Bancorp in May 1996 and also switched to a calendar reporting year from a June fiscal year in 1996.
Koranda said Clarendon Hills, Illinois-based MAF, a $3.23 billion asset thrift holding company, continues to look for other acquisitions.

"We are interested in doing more acquisitions," Koranda said. "There's nothing on the table right now. The trend of consolidation continues in our industry. We have our eyes open for any opportunities that may come around."
He stressed that the company is looking to make friendly deals.
Koranda indicated MAF would prefer to remain independent, although he said as a publicly traded company, it could not rule out being acquired.
"Our goal is to continue to grow this business and as long as we're having success at that, we think we can justify that (independent) position," he said.
Koranda said MAF has achieved about $4.2 million in annual savings from its merger with NS Bancorp and said another $400,000 to $500,000 in savings was possible.
MAF shares were up 1/4 at 40 Tuesday.
